newsitem.title: UK: OECD examining ways to curb tax competition - report.
newsitem.headline: OECD examining ways to curb tax competition - report.

text.p: The Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) has set up a taskforce to look at ways of curbing tax competition among member countries, the Financial Times reported on Monday.
The newspaper said a study was due to be completed by May 1998.
The project had been given priority funding after a first meeting of the taskforce and publication of the aims on the OECD's Internet site, said the Financial Times.

"It is understood that the study will look at non-OECD countries -- such as tax havens including the Cayman Islands -- as well as preferential corporate tax regimes in member states such as Ireland, the Netherlands and Belgium," the newspaper said.
The Financial Times reported that the OECD's Internet statement said the project's first task would be to "examine criteria for distinguishing between fair and harmful tax competition".
